newsitem.title: POLAND: Early Polish c.bank dlr-buying drives down zloty.
newsitem.headline: Early Polish c.bank dlr-buying drives down zloty.

text.p: The Polish zloty stabilised around 2.45 percent from the trading band centre in early trade after a $25 million central bank currency-buying intervention weakened the local unit this morning.

Soon after the zloty opened at 2.74/2.67 percent from parity, the central bank bought dollars around 2.70 percent and reversed a mainly speculative currency selling trend, driving down the zloty to Thursday's closing levels against the basket.
Dealers said the zloty was likely to hold below strong resistance around 2.5 percent from parity for the rest of the session unless foreigners purchased Polish T-bills on Friday.
"Foreigners have been quiet this morning, but if they arrive later in the day, the zloty could test higher levels again," said Tomasz Nowakowski dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

At 0915 the zloty was at 2.49/2.45 percent from the parity rate, against Thursday's close at 2.54/2.46 percent. It was at 3.1390/05 to the dollar, up from Thursday's 3.1460/80 and at 1.8285/95 to the mark, down from 1.8215/35.
The central bank bought dollars at 3.1336, 3.1340 zlotys.
On Thursday foreign investor bought Polish treasuries amid an estimated $230 million of central bank interventions, which weakened the zloty by 0.8 percentage points against the basket.
On the money market overnight rates increased slightly after the central bank announced a 1.2 billion zloty reverse repo and a 300 million zloty 273-day NBP-bill sale.
Overnight rates were quoted at 21.55/21.88 percent against opening's 21.50/21.80 percent and tomorrow/next were at 21.60/22.00 against opening's 21.50/21.90 percent.
